nodes.summary: Divisibility constraints on odd solutions of $(2^{k+1} - 1)(p^2 + p + 1) = 2^{k+1} p^2 + 2^b p + 1$. Let $b$ and $k$ be natural numbers and let $p$ be an odd natural number such that $(2^{k+1} - 1)(p^2 + p + 1) = 2^{k+1} p^2 + 2^b p + 1$. Then, as integers, $p$ divides $2^k - 1$ and $p + 1$ divides $2^b - 2$.
nodes.title: Divisibility constraints on odd solutions of $(2^{k+1} - 1)(p^2 + p + 1) = 2^{k+1} p^2 + 2^b p + 1$

nodes.summary: Odd solutions $p$ of $(2^{k+1} - 1)(p^2 + p + 1) = 2^{k+1} p^2 + 2^b p^2 + 1$ divide $2^k - 1$. Let $k$ and $b$ be positive natural numbers and let $p$ be an odd natural number such that $(2^{k+1} - 1)(p^2 + p + 1) = 2^{k+1} p^2 + 2^b p^2 + 1$. Then $p$ divides $2^k - 1$.
nodes.title: Odd solutions $p$ of $(2^{k+1} - 1)(p^2 + p + 1) = 2^{k+1} p^2 + 2^b p^2 + 1$ divide $2^k - 1$

nodes.summary: Let $a$ and $k$ be natural numbers with $1 \le a \le k$. If $2^{2k+2} + 2^{k+2} - 2^{a+2} - 7$ is the square of an integer, then $k = a = 1$.
nodes.title: Square values of the discriminant $2^{2k+2} + 2^{k+2} - 2^{a+2} - 7$

nodes.summary: Let $a$ and $b$ be natural numbers with $b \ge 1$. If $2^b + 1$ divides $3 \cdot 2^a + 1$, then $b = 2$.
nodes.title: If $b \ge 1$ and $2^b + 1$ divides $3 \cdot 2^a + 1$, then $b = 2$

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $n$, write $\sigma_k(n) = \sum_{e \mid n} e^k$. The number $n$ is deficient $F_k$-perfect when it is $[k,3]$-deficient-perfect, that is, when there is a divisor $d$ of $n$ with $d < n$ such that $\sigma_k(n) + d^k = n^k + 3n$.
nodes.title: Deficient $F_k$-perfect numbers

nodes.summary: The number $6$ is deficient $F$-perfect, and for every prime $p$ and every natural number $a$, if $2p^a$ is deficient $F$-perfect then $2p^a = 6$.
nodes.title: The only deficient $F$-perfect number of the form $2p^a$ is $6$

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and $a$ a natural number. If $2^a p$ is deficient $F$-perfect, then $p = 3$ and $a = 1$, so the number is $6$.
nodes.title: Deficient $F$-perfect numbers of the form $2^a p$

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, write $\sigma_2(n) = \sum_{e \mid n} e^2$. The number $n$ is deficient $F$-perfect when it is $[2,3]$-deficient-perfect, that is, when there is a divisor $d$ of $n$ with $d < n$ such that $\sigma_2(n) + d^2 = n^2 + 3n$.
nodes.title: Deficient $F$-perfect numbers

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and let $a$, $k$ and $\ell$ be natural numbers with $k \ge 2$. If $p^a$ is $[k,\ell]$-deficient-perfect, then $p = 2$ and $a = 1$.
nodes.title: $(k,\ell)$-deficient-perfect prime powers for $k \ge 2$

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and let $a$ and $\ell$ be natural numbers. If $p^a$ is $[2,\ell]$-deficient-perfect, then $\ell = 1$, and either $a = 2$, or $p = 2$ and $a = 1$.
nodes.title: $(2,\ell)$-deficient-perfect prime powers (corrected)

nodes.summary: For every natural number $k$, the number $2$ is $[k,1]$-deficient-perfect.
nodes.title: $2$ is $(k,1)$-deficient-perfect

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $k$, $\ell$ and $n$, write $\sigma_k(n) = \sum_{e \mid n} e^k$. The number $n$ is $[k,\ell]$-deficient-perfect when there is a divisor $d$ of $n$ with $d < n$ such that $\sigma_k(n) + d^k = n^k + \ell n$.
nodes.title: $(k,\ell)$-deficient-perfect numbers

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $\ell$ and $n$, say that $n$ is $[1,\ell]$-near-perfect when some divisor $d$ of $n$ with $d < n$ satisfies $\sigma(n) = n + d + \ell n$, where $\sigma(n)$ is the sum of the divisors of $n$. Then $18$ is $[1,1]$-near-perfect, and for every odd prime $p$ and all natural numbers $a$ and $\ell \ge 1$, if $2p^a$ is $[1,\ell]$-near-perfect then $2p^a = 18$.
nodes.title: The only $(1,\ell)$-near-perfect number of the form $2p^a$ is $18$

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $k$, $\ell$ and $n$, write $\sigma_k(n) = \sum_{e \mid n} e^k$. The number $n$ is $[k,\ell]$-near-perfect when there is a divisor $d$ of $n$ with $d < n$ such that $\sigma_k(n) = n^k + d^k + \ell n$.
nodes.title: $(k,\ell)$-near-perfect numbers

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $n$, the number $n$ is near $F_k$-perfect when it is $[k,3]$-near-perfect, that is, when some proper divisor $d$ of $n$ ($d \mid n$ and $d < n$) satisfies $\sigma_k(n) = n^k + d^k + 3n$, where $\sigma_k(n) = \sum_{e \mid n} e^k$ is the sum of the $k$-th powers of the divisors of $n$.
nodes.title: Near $F_k$-perfect numbers

nodes.summary: A natural number $n$ is near $F$-perfect when it is $[2,3]$-near-perfect, that is, when some proper divisor $d$ of $n$ ($d \mid n$ and $d < n$) satisfies $\sigma_2(n) = n^2 + d^2 + 3n$, where $\sigma_2(n) = \sum_{e \mid n} e^2$ is the sum of the squares of the divisors of $n$.
nodes.title: Near $F$-perfect numbers

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime, let $a$, $\ell$ and $d$ be natural numbers, and write $\sigma_1(m)$ for the sum of the divisors of $m$. Then $d$ is a proper divisor of $p^a$ ($d \mid p^a$ and $d < p^a$) with $\sigma_1(p^a) + d = p^a + \ell p^a$ if and only if $p = 2$, $\ell = 1$, $d = 1$ and $a \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Prime powers that are $(1,\ell)$-deficient-perfect with a given divisor

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime, let $a$, $k$, $\ell$ and $d$ be natural numbers with $k \ge 1$ and $\ell \ge 1$, and write $\sigma_k(m) = \sum_{e \mid m} e^k$. Then $d$ is a proper divisor of $p^a$ ($d \mid p^a$ and $d < p^a$) with $\sigma_k(p^a) = (p^a)^k + d^k + \ell p^a$ if and only if $2 \le a \le k$, $d = 1$ and $\ell = p^{k-a} \sum_{i=0}^{a-2} p^{ik}$.
nodes.title: Prime powers that are $(k,\ell)$-near-perfect

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime, let $a$, $\ell$ and $d$ be natural numbers with $\ell \ge 1$, and write $\sigma_2(m)$ for the sum of the squares of the divisors of $m$. Then $d$ is a proper divisor of $p^a$ ($d \mid p^a$ and $d < p^a$) with $\sigma_2(p^a) = (p^a)^2 + d^2 + \ell p^a$ if and only if $a = 2$, $\ell = 1$ and $d = 1$.
nodes.title: Prime powers that are $(2,\ell)$-near-perfect

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be an odd prime, let $a$, $k$, $\ell$ and $d$ be natural numbers with $k > 1$ and $\ell \ge 1$, and write $\sigma_k(m) = \sum_{e \mid m} e^k$. If $d$ is a proper divisor of $2p^a$ ($d \mid 2p^a$ and $d < 2p^a$) with $\sigma_k(2p^a) = (2p^a)^k + d^k + \ell \cdot 2p^a$, then $p^2 \mid 1 + 2^k$, and $a$ is even if and only if $d$ is odd.
nodes.title: A divisibility condition for near-perfect numbers $2p^a$

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $k$, $\ell$, $n$ and $d$, the number $n$ is $[k,\ell]$-deficient-perfect with divisor $d$ when $d$ is a proper divisor of $n$ ($d \mid n$ and $d < n$) and $\sigma_k(n) + d^k = n^k + \ell n$, where $\sigma_k(n) = \sum_{e \mid n} e^k$ is the sum of the $k$-th powers of the divisors of $n$.
nodes.title: $(k,\ell)$-deficient-perfect with a given divisor

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $k$, $\ell$, $n$ and $d$, the number $n$ is $[k,\ell]$-near-perfect with divisor $d$ when $d$ is a proper divisor of $n$ ($d \mid n$ and $d < n$) and $\sigma_k(n) = n^k + d^k + \ell n$, where $\sigma_k(n) = \sum_{e \mid n} e^k$ is the sum of the $k$-th powers of the divisors of $n$.
nodes.title: $(k,\ell)$-near-perfect with a given divisor

nodes.summary: Let $a \le k$ be natural numbers and let $p$ be a prime with $p(1 + 2^{k-a}) = 2^{k+1} - 2^a - 1$, that is, $p = (2^{k+1} - 2^a - 1)/(1 + 2^{k-a})$. Then $k < 2a$.
nodes.title: Prime solutions of $p(1 + 2^{k-a}) = 2^{k+1} - 2^a - 1$ satisfy $k < 2a$

nodes.summary: Let $k > 1$ be a natural number, let $p_1 \ne p_2$ be odd primes and let $a, b \ge 1$ be natural numbers such that $a + b$ is odd or both $a$ and $b$ are odd. Then $n = p_1^a p_2^b$ is not deficient $F_k$-perfect: there is no divisor $d$ of $n$ with $d < n$ and $\sigma_k(n) + d^k = n^k + 3n$, where $\sigma_k(n) = \sum_{e \mid n} e^k$.
nodes.title: No deficient $F_k$-perfect number $p_1^a p_2^b$ with $a + b$ odd or $a, b$ both odd

nodes.summary: Let $k > 1$ be a natural number, let $p_1 \ne p_2$ be odd primes and let $a$ be a natural number. Then $p_1^a p_2$ is not deficient $F_k$-perfect.
nodes.title: No deficient $F_k$-perfect number $p_1^a p_2$ with distinct odd primes

nodes.summary: Let $k > 1$ and let $s$ be a finite set of odd primes. Then $\prod_{p \in s} p$ is not deficient $F_k$-perfect.
nodes.title: No product of distinct odd primes is deficient $F_k$-perfect

nodes.summary: Let $k > 2$, let $p$ be an odd prime and let $a$ be a natural number. Then $2p^a$ is not deficient $F_k$-perfect.
nodes.title: No deficient $F_k$-perfect number of the form $2p^a$ for $k > 2$

nodes.summary: If $p$ is a prime, then $p$ is not deficient $F$-perfect.
nodes.title: No prime is deficient $F$-perfect

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be an odd prime. Then for all natural numbers $k$ and $\ell$, $p$ is not $[k,\ell]$-deficient-perfect.
nodes.title: Odd primes are not $(k,\ell)$-deficient-perfect

nodes.summary: Let $k$ and $\ell$ be natural numbers with $\ell \ge 1$ and let $p$ be a prime. Then $p$ is not $[k,\ell]$-near-perfect.
nodes.title: Primes are not $(k,\ell)$-near-perfect

nodes.summary: Let $k$ and $\ell$ be natural numbers with $\ell \ge 1$ and let $p$ be an odd prime. Then $2p$ is not $[k,\ell]$-near-perfect.
nodes.title: Twice an odd prime is not $(k,\ell)$-near-perfect

nodes.summary: Let $\ell$ and $a$ be natural numbers with $\ell \ge 1$, and let $p$ be an odd prime. Then $2^a p$ is not $[2,\ell]$-near-perfect.
nodes.title: No $(2,\ell)$-near-perfect number of the form $2^a p$

nodes.summary: Let $k > 1$, let $p_1 \ne p_2$ be odd primes and let $a, b \ge 1$ be natural numbers such that $a + b$ is odd or both $a$ and $b$ are odd. Then $p_1^a p_2^b$ is not near $F_k$-perfect.
nodes.title: No near $F_k$-perfect number $p_1^a p_2^b$ with $a + b$ odd or $a, b$ both odd

nodes.summary: Let $k > 1$, let $p_1$ and $p_2$ be distinct odd primes and let $a$ be a natural number. Then $p_1^a p_2$ is not near $F_k$-perfect.
nodes.title: No near $F_k$-perfect number of the form $p_1^a p_2$

nodes.summary: Let $k > 1$ and let $s$ be a finite set of odd primes. Then $\prod_{p \in s} p$ is not near $F_k$-perfect.
nodes.title: No product of distinct odd primes is near $F_k$-perfect

nodes.summary: For every prime $p$ and every natural number $a$, the number $n = 2p^a$ is not near $F$-perfect: there is no divisor $d$ of $n$ with $d < n$ and $\sigma_2(n) = n^2 + d^2 + 3n$, where $\sigma_2(n)$ is the sum of the squares of the divisors of $n$.
nodes.title: No near $F$-perfect number of the form $2p^a$

nodes.summary: For every prime $p$ and all natural numbers $a$ and $b$ with $b$ even, the number $n = 2^a p^b$ is not near $F$-perfect: there is no divisor $d$ of $n$ with $d < n$ and $\sigma_2(n) = n^2 + d^2 + 3n$, where $\sigma_2(n)$ is the sum of the squares of the divisors of $n$.
nodes.title: No near $F$-perfect number of the form $2^a p^b$ with $b$ even

nodes.summary: For every prime $p$ and every natural number $a$, the number $n = 2^a p$ is not near $F$-perfect: there is no divisor $d$ of $n$ with $d < n$ and $\sigma_2(n) = n^2 + d^2 + 3n$, where $\sigma_2(n)$ is the sum of the squares of the divisors of $n$.
nodes.title: No near $F$-perfect number of the form $2^a p$

nodes.summary: Let $k$, $\ell$, $a$ be natural numbers with $\ell \ge 1$ and let $p$ be an odd prime. Call $n$ $[k,\ell]$-deficient-perfect with divisor $d$ when $d$ divides $n$, $d < n$ and $\sigma_k(n) + d^k = n^k + \ell n$, where $\sigma_k(n)$ is the sum of the $k$-th powers of the divisors of $n$. Then $2^a p$ is not $[k,\ell]$-deficient-perfect with divisor $1$, and not with divisor $p$.
nodes.title: $2^a p$ is not $(k,\ell)$-deficient-perfect with divisor $1$ or $p$

nodes.summary: Let $k$, $\ell$, $a$ be natural numbers with $\ell \ge 1$ and $a \ge 2$, and let $p$ be an odd prime. Call $n$ $[k,\ell]$-near-perfect with divisor $d$ when $d$ divides $n$, $d < n$ and $\sigma_k(n) = n^k + d^k + \ell n$, where $\sigma_k(n)$ is the sum of the $k$-th powers of the divisors of $n$. Then $2^a p$ is not $[k,\ell]$-near-perfect with divisor $1$, and not with divisor $p$.
nodes.title: For $a \ge 2$, $2^a p$ is not $(k,\ell)$-near-perfect with divisor $1$ or $p$

nodes.summary: No odd solutions of $(2^{k+1} - 1)(p^2 + p + 1) = 2^{k+1} p^2 + 2^b p + 1$ for $2 \le b \le k - 1$. Let $b$ and $k$ be natural numbers with $2 \le b$ and $b + 1 \le k$, and let $p$ be an odd natural number. Then $(2^{k+1} - 1)(p^2 + p + 1) \ne 2^{k+1} p^2 + 2^b p + 1$.
nodes.title: No odd solutions of $(2^{k+1} - 1)(p^2 + p + 1) = 2^{k+1} p^2 + 2^b p + 1$ for $2 \le b \le k - 1$

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be an odd prime, let $k$ and $i$ be natural numbers with $i \le k$, let $m$ be $1$ or $2$, and let $n = 2^k p^2$. Then $\sigma(n) \ne 2n + 2^i + p^m$, where $\sigma$ is the sum-of-divisors function; that is, $n$ is not $2$-near perfect with omitted divisors $2^i$ and $p^m$.
nodes.title: No $2$-near perfect $2^k p^2$ with omitted divisors $2^i$ and $p$ or $p^2$

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be an odd prime, let $k$ be a natural number, and let $d_1 \ne d_2$ be divisors of $n = 2^k p^2$ with $\sigma(n) = 2n + d_1 + d_2$, where $\sigma$ denotes the sum of divisors. Then $d_1 + d_2 = -p^2 + (2^{k+1} - 1) p + (2^{k+1} - 1)$, and $d_1$ and $d_2$ have opposite parity.
nodes.title: Sum and parity of the omitted divisors of a $2$-near perfect $2^k p^2$

nodes.summary: For every prime $p$ and every natural number $a$, the number $n = p^a$ is neither deficient $F$-perfect nor near $F$-perfect: there is no divisor $d$ of $n$ with $d < n$ and $\sigma_2(n) + d^2 = n^2 + 3n$, and no divisor $d$ of $n$ with $d < n$ and $\sigma_2(n) = n^2 + d^2 + 3n$, where $\sigma_2(n)$ is the sum of the squares of the divisors of $n$.
nodes.title: No prime power is deficient $F$-perfect or near $F$-perfect

nodes.summary: Let $a \le k$ be natural numbers and let $p$ be a prime with $p(1 + 2^{k-a}) = 2^{k+1} - 2^a - 1$, that is, $p = (2^{k+1} - 2^a - 1)/(1 + 2^{k-a})$. Then $k = a + 2$, $2^k p / 2^a = 4p$, $5p = 2^{a+3} - 2^a - 1$, and $a \equiv 3 \pmod 4$.
nodes.title: Classification of prime solutions of $p(1 + 2^{k-a}) = 2^{k+1} - 2^a - 1$

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be an odd prime, let $k$ be a natural number and let $n = 2^k p$. Suppose that $n$ is strongly $2$-near perfect, that is, $\sigma(n) = 2n + d + n/d$ for some divisor $d$ of $n$, where $\sigma$ is the sum-of-divisors function. Then there is a natural number $a \le k$ with $p(1 + 2^{k-a}) = 2^{k+1} - 2^a - 1$, that is, $p = (2^{k+1} - 2^a - 1)/(1 + 2^{k-a})$.
nodes.title: Strongly $2$-near perfect numbers of the form $2^k p$

nodes.summary: Odd solutions $p$ of $(2^{k+1} - 1)(p^2 + p + 1) = 2^{k+1} p^2 + 2^b p^2 + 1$ satisfy $p + 1 \mid 2^b + 2$. Let $k$ and $b$ be positive natural numbers and let $p$ be an odd natural number such that $(2^{k+1} - 1)(p^2 + p + 1) = 2^{k+1} p^2 + 2^b p^2 + 1$. Then, as integers, $p + 1$ divides $2^b + 2$.
nodes.title: Odd solutions $p$ of $(2^{k+1} - 1)(p^2 + p + 1) = 2^{k+1} p^2 + 2^b p^2 + 1$ satisfy $p + 1 \mid 2^b + 2$

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 1$, let $p$ be a prime and let $n = 2^k p$. Suppose $d_1 \ne d_2$ are divisors of $n$ with $\sigma(n) = 2n + d_1 + d_2$, where $\sigma$ is the sum-of-divisors function (that is, $n$ is $2$-near perfect with omitted divisors $d_1, d_2$). Then, after possibly swapping $d_1$ and $d_2$, one of the following holds, where all equations are between integers: (1) $p = 2^k - 1$, $d_1 = 1$ and $d_2 = p$; (2) for…
nodes.title: $2$-near perfect numbers of the form $2^k p$

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be an odd prime and let $b, k$ be integers with $1 \le b \le k$. If $n = 2^k p^2$ satisfies $\sigma(n) = 2n + 1 + 2^b p^2$, where $\sigma$ is the sum-of-divisors function (that is, $n$ is $2$-near perfect with omitted divisors $1$ and $2^b p^2$), then $n = 36$ and $2^b p^2 = 18$.
nodes.title: $2$-near perfect $2^k p^2$ with omitted divisors $1$ and $2^b p^2$

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be an odd prime, let each of $m$ and $j$ be $1$ or $2$, and let $b, k$ be integers with $1 \le b \le k$. If $n = 2^k p^2$ satisfies $\sigma(n) = 2n + p^m + 2^b p^j$, where $\sigma$ is the sum-of-divisors function (that is, $n$ is $2$-near perfect with omitted divisors $p^m$ and $2^b p^j$), then $n = 200$.
nodes.title: $2$-near perfect $2^k p^2$ with omitted divisors $p^m$ and $2^b p^j$

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be an odd prime, let $k$ be a natural number and let $i \ne j$ be natural numbers with $i \le k$ and $j \le k$. If $n = 2^k p^2$ satisfies $\sigma(n) = 2n + 2^i + 2^j$, where $\sigma$ is the sum-of-divisors function (that is, $n$ is $2$-near perfect with omitted divisors $2^i$ and $2^j$), then $n = 18$ and either $i = 0, j = 1$ or $i = 1, j = 0$, so the omitted divisors are $1$ and $2$.
nodes.title: $2$-near perfect $2^k p^2$ whose omitted divisors are powers of $2$

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime, let $k$ be a natural number and let $n = 2^k p^2$. If $n$ has divisors $d_1 \ne d_2$ with $\sigma(n) = 2n + d_1 + d_2$, where $\sigma$ is the sum-of-divisors function (that is, $n$ is $2$-near perfect with omitted divisors $d_1, d_2$), then $n$ is $18$, $36$ or $200$.
nodes.title: $2$-near perfect numbers of the form $2^k p^2$

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
